method.agent_mode: MSI with DNSFILTER=1, VDOM=WebActionsSandbox, server via guest-loopback HTTP relay to the homologation server; no block page, CA, anti-bypass, USB or application controls
method.dns_probe: Clear-DnsClientCache; Resolve-DnsName -Type A -DnsOnly -NoHostsFile -QuickTimeout through the system resolver (agent NRPT); block answer is 0.0.0.0
method.ack: endpoint applied_digest/config_version/last_error read from PostgreSQL after each publication
method.events: block_events deltas per domain/action/reason/category plus web_event_batches count/received_at; each scenario policy adds a unique blocked canary probed last, so a no-event claim is accepted only after a later event reached the server
method.dedup: same domain re-probed only after 65 s (agent deduplicates per minute)
method.invalid_digest_injection: the server refuses to serve a category file whose bytes do not match its digest, so the guest relay flipped the last byte of the sports file while a guest-local flag existed
method.browsers: retail Chrome (CDP) and Firefox 158.0.1 (BiDi), fresh profiles on the guest local disk (C:\openems-browser-profiles), outputs on the mapped results folder, 180 s global deadline, TLS validation unchanged
method.sandbox_rule: three fresh guests, one per round; no round repeated in the same guest; each guest removed the agent before being stopped

isolation_finding: The Sandbox NAT DNS forwards to the host resolver. The host's own agent (Default policy, hosts file) answers 127.0.0.1 for example.com/www.example.com/neverssl.com. In rounds 1-2 every example.com/www.example.com answer is therefore loopback from upstream: the guest agent did forward them (no 0.0.0.0, no event), but those rows were not attributable and were repeated in round 3 with www.ietf.org and www.rfc-editor.org. The probe now classifies loopback answers separately.
